summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of Leave Year Configuration feature. All 12 backend pytest cases pass (GET /tenants/me, PUT /tenants/settings with Federal/Texas/UK/Calendar presets, invalid month/day validation, /leave-balances returns correct fiscal year range for Calendar/Federal/UK FY). Frontend UI verified end-to-end: Leave Year Configuration card renders on /tools/branding, month/day dropdowns work, all 4 presets (Jan 1, Oct 1, Jul 1, Apr 1) update state and highlight active preset, Save Settings persists via PUT /tenants/settings and shows 'Leave year settings saved' toast, Reset to Calendar Year button works. Leave Balances panel on /battalion-chief/vacation correctly reflects fiscal year change: after setting Federal FY (Oct 1), header shows '2025-2026 Leave Balances' with badge '2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30'. Reset back to calendar year post-test.
critical_code_review_comments: LeaveYearSettings.js line 83: `const currentYear = today.year || today.getFullYear();` - `today.year` is undefined on a Date object; harmless due to `||` fallback but is dead code and misleading. Just use `today.getFullYear()`.

Backend /leave-balances uses naive `datetime.now()` (server local time) to determine current fiscal year; consider using tenant timezone-aware date to avoid edge cases near fiscal year boundary in different timezones.

leave_year_start_day validation is only bounds-checked 1-31; a value like Feb 30 will still be stored and cause `datetime(y, 2, 30)` to raise ValueError inside /leave-balances (500). Recommend validating day against days-in-month on the backend, similar to how the frontend clamps it in handleMonthChange.
